todos.note: `bash curriculum/evals/scripts/source-freshness.sh --target 2026-09-25 curriculum/lectures/skills-from-the-frontier.md` really run this pass → exit 1, '1 block · 1 warn · 2 info · 6 ok'. The BLOCK is L115's `[checked:never result:NEEDED due:asap]` stamp on the Ramp/Levick 99.7%-vs-99.5% divergence inside the backing block's Flagged/OODA section — not a Sources-ledger entry, and the file's own text says 'Nothing owed above the divider'. The shipped student-facing body (L1-38) makes no Ramp claim at all, so no harm reaches students; the debt properly belongs to `observations/ramp.md`. Worth two things: (1) resolve the Levick figure there eventually; (2) source-freshness.sh's grep doesn't distinguish a Sources-ledger stamp from a Flagged-section research-debt stamp, so it reports this file as cohort-blocking when it isn't — a §45-shaped false-positive (detector vocabulary narrower than corpus writing convention) worth a scoping fix, not something this read-only pass can apply.

Body names the authored skill's path as bare `test-strategy` (no SUT suffix). Real students each have their own home directory so this is harmless to them, but check_platform_and_boundaries.md §30 requires the actual EXERCISE authoring-prompt (a different file, out of this judge's scope) to namespace by SUT to avoid multi-run mechanical-harness collisions — worth confirming that exercise file does the namespacing, not this lecture.
